content.title: About
content.content: Fudgesicle is a frozen dessert pop on a stick made from creamy ice cream flavored like fudge. It is coated with a thin chocolate shell and often contains bits of nuts or caramel. The treat is popular as a refreshing sweet snack in warm weather.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first fudgesicle appeared in the United States in the 1970s as an experimental version of the classic popsicle.
Original recipes used real fudge paste, but today many manufacturers use flavorings.
Fudgesicles are typically sold in bite‑size portions that are easy to hold without a spoon.
Some countries now offer a vegan version made with coconut milk.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and the immune system.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Sugar and fat give a rapid boost of energy, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Probiotic content (in some versions)
items.content: Certain recipes include live cultures that may benefit gut health.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: Some varieties contain nuts, posing a risk for allergic individuals.

items.title: Brain freeze
items.content: Eating it straight from the freezer can cause a sudden headache known as brain freeze.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fudgesicles are eaten directly from the freezer, holding the stick. Letting it sit for a minute allows the chocolate coating to soften. Serve with fresh berries or sprinkle with nut crumble for extra texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower in the original packaging. Over long periods sugar may crystallize, making the texture slightly grainy.
